Addressed by #45789. OpenAI Responses now closes the previous reasoning fragment before opening a new summary part, normalizes missing and delayed item boundaries, and turns genuinely overlapping distinct reasoning items into typed invalid-provider-output failures rather than internal defects. Focused lifecycle regressions cover the reported start-before-end sequence. Closing as resolved on the v2 branch.

Addressed by #45091. The updater now remembers the last successfully installed version so a long-running service does not repeatedly reinstall it, and npm updates use a scoped temporary cache that is removed afterward. The updater-service regression exercises repeated checks and fails with three installs when the fix is removed versus one with it applied. Closing as resolved on the v2 branch.
Keeps happening on OpenCode Web and Desktop 1.18.23

Still reproduces on **1.18.23** (latest release) — I just hit the snowball variant: a rate-limited turn persisted a zero-part assistant message with `error: APIError`, and every subsequent request failed with `the message at position 772 with role 'assistant' must not be empty`, each retry appending yet another empty artifact message (391 → had to delete 3 rows from `opencode.db` to recover).

The guards currently on `dev` (skip zero-part messages, skip errored messages, skip step-start-only messages) cover the zero-part case, but three shapes still replay as empty assistant content:

1. **Aborted turn with a `patch` part** — the abort carve-out treats any non-`step-start`/`reasoning` part as content, so `[step-start, reasoning, patch]` survives; `patch` never serializes, leaving a reasoning-only message that OpenAI-compatible converters turn into `content: ""`. This is the exact shape in this issue's report.
2. **Reasoning-only turn with no `error` field** (crash/disconnect before the error is persisted) — the error filter never runs.
3. **Turn with only empty text parts** (`text: ""`).

Verified against `dev` by calling `MessageV2.toModelMessages` directly with these shapes — all three still produce empty assistant messages.

PR with a fix + regression tests: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/45839

The fix tightens the abort carve-out to count only model-visible parts (non-empty text or tool) and drops any assistant turn that produces no model-visible content at conversion time — so it also heals already-bricked sessions without a DB migration.

This is fixed in https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/45839 — the text branch now skips empty text parts during conversion (the Anthropic signed-reasoning space substitution still runs first, so signed separators are unaffected). Verified with regression tests plus a replay of a real bricked session's history.

Still relevant and still applicable to `dev`.

The linked issue (#39163) is open and the underlying gap hasn't changed: a SHA pin on `anomalyco/opencode/github` pins the composite wrapper only — `action.yml` still `curl`s the installer from opencode.ai at run time and installs whatever the latest CLI release is. Anyone pinning by SHA for supply-chain reasons currently gets a pin that doesn't cover the thing that actually executes.

The change is one commit, ~10 lines in `github/action.yml`: run the `install` script already checked out at the pinned ref, and pass an optional `version` input through to it as `VERSION`, which the installer already supports. `./install` is sha256-identical to what opencode.ai serves, so this changes where the script comes from, not what it does. Default behaviour without the new input is unchanged.

Verified both paths on an `ubuntu-latest` runner (pinned `1.18.6` while `1.18.7` was latest, and no input → `1.18.7`); details are in the PR description.

No review comments were left before it was closed, so nothing is outstanding on my side. Happy to rebase if `dev` has moved. Requesting reopen.

Read the code — this is the contribution column doing its (poorly-labeled) job, not a math bug.

In `packages/console/app/src/routes/workspace/[id]/go/lite-section.tsx` the percentage column renders `row.contributionPercent` from `buildLiteUsageBreakdown` (`packages/console/app/src/lib/lite-usage.ts`): each row's share of the **total window usage**, allocated by quota-weighted largest-remainder so the column sums to the window's overall usage percent. It is not `usage / per-model quota` — the quota column is display-only context, which is exactly the misreading this table invites.

Two ways to fix the confusion, happy to send either:

1. **Change the percentage to `usage / quota` per row** (what every reader expects next to those two columns). Sum will no longer be 100%.
2. **Keep the contribution math, fix the label** — e.g. rename the column to "share of window usage" in the i18n strings so it can't be read as per-model utilization.

Preference? Option 1 is a small change in the same files.

Opened #45888 with the conservative first step (CRLF detection now requires every newline to be CRLF, so mixed files match as LF and LF regions become editable).

Two design questions remain for the full fix (editing the CRLF region of a mixed file), and I'd rather not guess:

1. **Policy**: should edits preserve the file's mixed endings byte-for-byte, or normalize the touched region (or the whole file) to the dominant ending? Preserving keeps diffs minimal but perpetuates mixed files; normalizing makes diffs larger but converges the file.
2. **Scope**: normalized-search span mapping touches a destructive write path, and `replaceAll` counting plus the uniqueness check would need to run consistently on the normalized copy. Happy to implement once the policy is settled.
